citeAs: Etash Guha, Ryan Marten, Sedrick Keh, Negin Raoof, Georgios Smyrnis, et al. (2025). Data Recipes for Reasoning Models. arXiv:2506.04178.
creator: Ryan Marten (BespokeLabs.ai)
description: A 1K-sample subset of the OpenThoughts dataset series — open-source datasets for training reasoning models via supervised fine-tuning. The OpenThoughts datasets contain question-thinking-tokens-answer triplets across math, code, and science domains, generated by distilling reasoning traces from teacher models such as DeepSeek-R1 and QwQ-32B.
name: OpenThoughts-1k-sample
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Reasoning traces (answers) are generated by querying teacher models (DeepSeek-R1 or QwQ-32B) on each question. Multiple answers per question are sampled (up to 16x). For OpenThoughts-114K, answer matching and unit tests were used to verify math and code responses, filtering out reasoning traces with incorrect answers. OpenThoughts3 does not rely on any form of verification.
rai:dataBiases: The dataset is limited to math, code, and science domains. Questions are sourced from a small number of high-quality sources (top 1-2 sources per domain), which may introduce source-specific biases. The dataset uses English-only filtering for answers. Decontamination removes samples similar to evaluation benchmarks, which may introduce selection bias.
rai:dataCollection: Questions are sourced from existing datasets and newly generated datasets across math, code, and science domains. Answers (reasoning traces) are generated by distilling from teacher models (primarily DeepSeek-R1 or QwQ-32B). The pipeline involves: (1) sourcing questions from existing and newly generated datasets, (2) mixing questions from top-performing sources, (3) filtering for high-quality questions using fastText or LLMs, (4) deduplicating questions and sampling multiple answers per question, (5) filtering out low-quality answers using LLM verification or majority consensus, and (6) selecting the best teacher model.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Questions sourced from existing datasets including StackExchange CodeGolf, OpenCodeReasoning, NuminaMath-1.5, OpenMath-2-Math, StackExchange Physics, and organic chemistry PDFs. Answers are reasoning traces generated by teacher models (DeepSeek-R1 or QwQ-32B) in response to these questions.
rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Web Scraping, Software Collection, Others
rai:dataLimitations: The dataset does not include data for reinforcement learning. The paper did not explore staged SFT or curriculum learning. Safety alignment is degraded when models are fine-tuned on this data. The dataset focuses only on math, code, and science domains. Distilled reasoning models trained on this data still show generalization deficits (strong performance fluctuations on reasoning-invariant problem variations).
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Multiple answers per question are sampled from teacher models (1x, 4x, or 16x). Exact and fuzzy deduplication of questions using Indel similarity (LCS metric). Questions are filtered by LLM-assessed difficulty or response length. For the final OpenThoughts3 pipeline: exact deduplication for math and science, no deduplication for code, and 16x answer sampling for all domains.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Decontamination against evaluation benchmarks using two methods: (1) Indel similarity (Normalized LCS metric, threshold 75%) and (2) N-gram-based similarity (N=13, using Qwen2-7B-Instruct tokenizer). Samples marked contaminated by either method are discarded. The decontamination algorithm achieves 99.6% true negative rate.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset enables open-source development of reasoning models, democratizing access to training data that was previously proprietary. However, fine-tuning on reasoning data inadvertently degrades safety alignment: OpenThinker3-7B trained on this data shows increased harmfulness rates (55.5 on Harmbench vs 14.5 for the base Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct), indicating a trade-off between reasoning capabilities and safety.
rai:dataUseCases: Supervised fine-tuning (SFT) of language models to develop reasoning capabilities in math, code, and science domains. The dataset is intended for training reasoning models that can output long chains of thought (thinking tokens) during inference.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: DeepSeek-R1 (teacher model for generating reasoning traces), QwQ-32B (teacher model), GPT-4o-mini (for question filtering, difficulty scoring, answer verification, and question generation), GPT-4.1-mini and GPT-4.1-nano (for response length filtering), FastText classifiers (for question and answer filtering), Gemini-2.0-flash-lite (for OCR of PDF content), OpenAI text-embedding-3-large (for embedding-based filtering)

evidence.name: We share open artifacts with the community via openthoughts.ai.
evidence.description: The goal of the OpenThoughts project is to create open-source datasets for training reasoning models. After initial explorations, our OpenThoughts2-1M dataset led to OpenThinker2-32B, the first model trained on public reasoning data to match DeepSeek-R1-Distill-32B on standard reasoning benchmarks such as AIME and LiveCodeBench.
evidence.url: We release our model and our dataset as part of a collection on Hugging Face. Our OpenThinker3-7B model can be found in https://huggingface.co/open-thoughts/OpenThinker3-7B, and our dataset can be found in https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-thoughts/OpenThoughts3-1.2M.
evidence.creator: Etash Guha*1,2, Ryan Marten*3, Sedrick Keh*4, Negin Raoof*5, Georgios Smyrnis*6
evidence.publisher: We are launching the OpenThoughts project to create state-of-the-art open reasoning datasets by exploring the rich design space in reasoning SFT datasets, specifically focusing on how to identify the best questions and corresponding answers that encourage reasoning. Beginning with BespokeStratos-17K (Bespoke-Labs, 2025), we have progressed through four generations of releases, culminating in OpenThoughts3-1.2M and OpenThinker3-7B. We share open artifacts with the community via openthoughts.ai.
evidence.inLanguage: Removing Non-English Answers : Ask GPT-4o-mini whether a provided answer contains only English.
evidence.isLiveDataset: We release our model and our dataset as part of a collection on Hugging Face. Our OpenThinker3-7B model can be found in https://huggingface.co/open-thoughts/OpenThinker3-7B, and our dataset can be found in https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-thoughts/OpenThoughts3-1.2M.
evidence.citeAs: arXiv:2506.04178v2 [cs.LG] 5 Jun 2025 DATA RECIPES FOR REASONING MODELS Etash Guha*1,2, Ryan Marten*3, Sedrick Keh*4, Negin Raoof*5, Georgios Smyrnis*6
evidence.rai:dataCollection: We investigate (1) sourcing questions from existing and newly generated datasets, (2) mixing questions from the top-performing sources, (3) filtering for high-quality questions using fastText or LLMs, (4) deduplicating questions and sampling multiple answers per question, (5) filtering out low-quality answers using LLM verification or majority consensus, and (6) selecting the best teacher model.
evidence.rai:dataCollectionType: We can broadly categorize our question sourcing techniques into three types: (1) Fully synthetic – an existing LLM generates questions with little-to-no seed material. (2) Semi-synthetic – an LLM uses existing data sources such as CommonCrawl or FineWeb as seeds to form questions. (3) Non-synthetic – humans write the questions. These questions often arise from online forums, contests, chatbot interactions, and other sources.
evidence.rai:dataCollectionRawData: For code, CodeGolf questions from StackExchange and competitive coding questions from OpenCodeReasoning (Ahmad et al., 2025) perform well, achieving scores of 25.3 and 27.5 on average on code benchmarks. For math, both LLM-generated questions in openmath-2-math (Toshniwal et al., 2024) and human-written questions in NuminaMath (LI et al., 2024) score the highest.
evidence.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: We also decontaminate our datasets against our benchmarks by removing samples with high similarity. Details for this process are in Appendix F. Our final decontamination algorithm only misses 12 questions out of 3092 manually contaminated items, representing a 99.6% true negative rate.
evidence.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Our tooling utilizes answer matching and unit tests to verify math and code responses, filtering out reasoning traces with incorrect answers. OpenThoughts3 does not rely on any form of verification.
evidence.rai:machineAnnotationTools: We use GPT-4o-mini for all sources that we generate which require an LLM. Finally, we use DeepSeek-R1 to generate responses for each question, even if a pre-existing answer exists.
evidence.rai:dataUseCases: Our goal is to create the best dataset of question-response pairs for SFT reasoning. The best dataset is the one that produces the highest-performing model.
evidence.rai:dataSocialImpact: In Table 30, we observe that supervised fine-tuning on reasoning inadvertently degrades the pre-existing safety alignment of Qwen2.5 models, consistent with prior findings Qi et al. (2023). Notably, OpenThinker3-7B was trained without any explicit safety-tuning or alignment-focused data, which likely contributes to its degraded safety performance.
evidence.rai:dataLimitations: This work has several limitations. We did not explore datasets for reinforcement learning, a standard training regime for building reasoning models. Within the SFT realm, we did not explore the use of staged SFT or curriculum learning to further improve performance.
evidence.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Our final pipeline uses 16×answers per question for all domains. It uses exact deduplication for math and science and no deduplication for code.
evidence.rai:dataBiases: Selecting questions from a small number (top 1 or 2) of high-quality sources leads to better downstream performance compared to optimizing for diversity (i.e., top 8 or 16 sources).
